newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel oil business thin, ARA barges pick up.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel oil business thin, ARA barges pick up.

text.p: European high sulphur barge prices picked up on Thursday from the previous day's late lows but business was again very thin, traders said.
Amongst the other grades, only low sulphur straight-run appeared lively.
One barge trade was heard done on Thursday morning at $82 fob ARA. Bunker demand was reported moderate.

The sharp price swings over the last two days have unsettled some in the market, with low volumes making values particularly prone to volatility. Barges were traded as high at $87 on Tuesday and hit a low of $79.50 on Wednesday.
Overall morning markets were quiet both in the Mediterranean and in the north.
High sulphur cargoes were little discussed and buyers complaining that posted prices were far from reality.
"The numbers are now more used to price other deals than to set a value for real activity," said one player.
A cargo of low sulphur straight-run was heard sold by a British major to Milford Haven at a price around $104 cif on Wednesday.
Offer prices on the grade have now climbed to around $100 fob, with sellers spurred by perceived U.S. demand.
